report.answer_text:
Baby KJ Muldoon received k-abe (kayjayguran abengcemeran), a personalised CRISPR adenine base-editing therapy designed to correct a specific mutation in his *CPS1* gene. The treatment was infused intravenously, using lipid nanoparticles to deliver the editor to his liver cells. His first infusion was on February 25, 2025. (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov)
KJ was born with severe carbamoyl phosphate synthetase 1 (CPS1) deficiency, a rare disorder that prevents the body from clearing toxic ammonia effectively. The May 2025 report found that after treatment he could tolerate more dietary protein and needed less ammonia-lowering medication, though longer follow-up was needed. (beta.nih.gov)
